svg.title: How two plug-in steps form a loop and three ways to stop it
svg.desc: Top half: the naive design. Lina sets a case to High at depth 1. Step U1 on Update of case updates the urgent flag of a work order at depth 2. Step U2 on Update of work order updates the priority of the case at depth 3. That starts U1 again at depth 4, and so on until the platform aborts at depth 8 with an infinite loop error and rolls everything back. Bottom half: the three brakes. First, registration: filtering attributes so that a step only starts for the column it reacts to. Second, state: compare pre-image and post-image and write only values that differ, so the second round finds nothing to do. Third, a guard token in SharedVariables that nested operations read through ParentContext, which skips the echo without any data call. With the brakes, the chain ends at depth 2 when the case changes first and at depth 3 when a work order changes first.
svg.text: Naive design: each step writes the row the other step listens to
"Submitted" is enough to start a step again: nothing changes any more, yet the loop continues. Everything rolls back.
Writes send only the changed column,
Does not stop: a true cycle.
U1: query only work orders whose
Urgent differs from the wanted value.
U2: pre vs post image; escalate only
if the case is not already High.
set by U1 before it writes; U2 reads it
once: no query at all for the echo.
Depth 1: Lina's update → U1 (token set) → Depth 2: work order updates → U2 sees the token and returns. The chain ends at depth 2.
Sami marks a work order urgent → U2 (token set) escalates the case → U1 flags only sibling work orders that differ → their U2 runs see the token.
Learn: do not take any dependency on Depth. The same step is reached at depth 2 or 3 by a flow, another plug-in or an import path,
and would silently skip real work. Depth belongs to the platform's loop detector (maximum 8 within one hour).
